title: Mirzapur The Movie a Clean Hit on Day 10, Enters 2026's Top 5 Grossers
excerpt: Ten days in, the Prime Video spin-off has collected ₹189.67 crore net in India on a ₹90 crore budget — a 110.74% return on investment that trade trackers call a clean hit, making it Bollywood's fourth such verdict of 2026.
body:
• Mirzapur The Movie collected ₹13.1 crore net on its second Sunday (day 10), taking its 10-day domestic total to ₹189.67 crore net (₹223.81 crore gross), per Koimoi.
  • On a reported ₹90 crore budget, the film's return on investment is 110.74% — a clean "hit" verdict, and only the fourth Bollywood film of 2026 to earn one, after Dhurandhar 2, Awarapan 2 and Hanuman Ansh.
  • It has passed Dhamaal 4 (₹177.92 crore) to become the year's fifth highest-grossing Bollywood release in India, with Bhooth Bangla (₹199.23 crore) next in its sights.
  • Worldwide, the film stands at about ₹266–270 crore gross, with ₹46 crore from overseas markets led by North America.

Ten days into its theatrical run, Mirzapur The Movie has moved from a strong opening to a certified commercial success. The crime thriller collected ₹13.1 crore net in India on its second Sunday, September 13, and closed its first ten days at ₹189.67 crore net, according to trade tracker Koimoi.

Produced on a reported budget of ₹90 crore, the film has generated ₹99.67 crore in profit over its production cost — a 110.74% return on investment, and a clean hit verdict by Koimoi's parameters. It is the fourth Bollywood release of 2026 to earn one.

A second weekend that held its line

After a first week of ₹153.77 crore net, the film dipped to ₹9.5 crore on its second Friday — a standard second-weekend drop — then rebounded to ₹13.3 crore on day 9 and ₹13.1 crore on day 10, for a second weekend of ₹35.9 crore. The recovery came against direct competition — the new release Haiwaan and the ongoing run of Hanuman Ansh — yet Mirzapur stayed the second choice for Hindi moviegoers, per Koimoi.

From Prime Video to the big screen

The numbers carry an asterisk that makes them more remarkable: Mirzapur began as a Prime Video series, not a film franchise. The movie is an offshoot of the show's first season, with Pankaj Tripathi, Ali Fazal and Divyenndu reprising Kaleen Bhaiya, Guddu Pandit and Munna Tripathi. Ravi Kishan joins as Babloo Babua, a Rajasthani strongman eyeing the throne; Jitendra Kumar takes over as Babloo Pandit from Vikrant Massey.

Directed by Gurmmeet Singh from a screenplay by Puneet Krishna, the film is presented by Amazon MGM Studios and Excel Entertainment, and produced by Ritesh Sidhwani and Farhan Akhtar. Turning a streaming property into theatrical footfalls was considered a genuine gamble.

The opening weekend suggested the gamble was working: ₹93 crore net, the third-biggest Hindi opening weekend of 2026. The first day's ₹25.75 crore bettered the day-one hauls of Saiyaara (₹22 crore) and Awarapan 2 (₹21.5 crore), per Cinema Express — impressive for a film headlined by character actors.

"For Mirzapur – The Movie, however, the bigger story is not just the ranking. It is the fact that a franchise born and nurtured on streaming has now made a convincing theatrical statement."

— Bollywood Hungama

What the verdict means for 2026

The hit-verdict club of 2026 shows where Bollywood's money is: Dhurandhar 2 towers at ₹1,186.32 crore net, Border 2 at ₹362.76 crore, Hanuman Ansh at ₹214.63 crore — and Mirzapur now slots fifth at ₹189.67 crore, ahead of Dhamaal 4's ₹177.92 crore. Within reach: the ₹200-crore net club and Bhooth Bangla's ₹199.23 crore for the fourth spot on the year's domestic chart.

The broader implication is about franchise filmmaking drawn from streaming. Mirzapur's 110%+ ROI suggests that for a brand with a devoted audience, the theatre adds a layer the living room cannot — a result other studios will study closely.

The overseas leg

The diaspora audience showed up, if modestly. Overseas markets have contributed about ₹46 crore by day 10, per Sacnilk — roughly a fifth of the worldwide gross. North America was part of the story from the start: the opening weekend took $2.1 million overseas, led by North America and the Middle East, according to Zoom TV. North America alone contributed $670,000 across the first two days, per Sacnilk's territory data.

What to watch next

Two numbers frame the rest of the run: ₹200 crore net, which the film should cross within two days, and Bhooth Bangla's ₹199.23 crore, the barrier to fourth place on 2026's domestic chart. Weekday holds in the strongholds — Uttar Pradesh and Bihar drove the early surge, per Zoom TV — will decide whether the lifetime total pushes toward ₹250 crore.

The longer question is whether Excel Entertainment and Amazon MGM treat this as a one-off experiment or a template. A hit at 110% ROI from a streaming-born property is the kind of result that reshapes greenlight meetings. The throne of Mirzapur, it turns out, extends beyond the small screen.
